data.title: You can move between related forms
data.subtitle: Next, make the relation–relationship distinction precise.

blocks.title: relationship
blocks.content: Use relationship for how people, groups, or organisations connect: my relationship with my parents; the relationship between two teams.

blocks.title: relation
blocks.content: Use relation in formal reference or for a general connection: in relation to the advert; a relation between price and demand.

blocks.title: Family and adjective forms
blocks.content: A relative is a family member. Related means connected and is followed by to.

data.instruction: Read both sections and choose the main idea.

stimulus.content: Two short accounts show how relationships shaped Maya while she was growing up.

sections.title: Learning with friends
sections.content: At the start of primary school, Maya found it difficult to relate to unfamiliar children. Noor was accommodating: she changed the rules of a playground game so Maya could join. Their daily interaction made the friendship rewarding and helped both children learn to cooperate.

sections.title: Learning at home
sections.content: Maya also had frequent conflict with her older sibling. Their parents did not remove every disagreement; they helped the children explain their feelings and nurture a stronger bond. By adolescence, the rivalry had weakened and the two could rely on each other.
